extracted.intended_audience: aspiring video game writers, narrative designers, game developers, and students of game writing
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and descriptive criteria for writing scripts and narratives for video games, covering roles (pitch writer, narrative designer, script writer), genre-specific constraints (non-linearity, interactivity), pitch structure, and industry practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-linear and interactive nature of games
rubrics_metrics.description: Video game writing differs from writing for other arts, due to the non-linear and interactive nature of most video games.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers must account for player agency and branching structures; narrative must be designed to function across non-linear play rather than a single linear progression. This difference is repeatedly emphasized as a core constraint that separates game writing from film or stage writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborate closely with designers and voice actors
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of interactivity and mechanics, video game writers must work closely with video game designers and voice actors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writing is integrated into the design team during pre-production; writers coordinate with designers to ensure narrative fits mechanics and with voice actors for performance delivery. The article repeatedly highlights collaboration as essential to the craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle diverse types of in-game text
rubrics_metrics.description: There are many differing types of text in video games in comparison to stage shows or movies, including written text, foreign or made-up languages, and often situation-based information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers should be prepared to produce UI/UX text, lore entries, invented languages, item descriptions, contextual situation text, and other non-dialogue written elements that convey story or gameplay information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team-based role differentiation for larger (AAA) projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Especially when developing Triple A games, more than one writer will be required to create the game, split into different roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect specialization (pitch writers, narrative designers, script writers, localization writers, etc.) and coordination across multiple writers; responsibilities and scope will be divided according to role and project needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize mechanics vs. narrative and avoid ludonarrative dissonance
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority is often given to interactive play mechanics over narrative which can lead to ludonarrative dissonance: a situation when ludic and narrative elements are opposed to each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers should design narrative and mechanics in alignment; be aware that designers may deprioritize plot and take steps to prevent conflict between what the game asks the player to do and what the story says they are doing. The article cites examples and discussion (e.g., Clint Hocking) highlighting this anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core writer responsibilities during development
rubrics_metrics.description: People who write video games ... create the main plot of a video game but can also focus on the dialogue, the character creation and development or the worldbuilding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers may be tasked with creating overarching story arcs, scripting character dialogue, developing character backstories, building game world lore, and later fixing narrative issues as the game's design changes during development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch document components and metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: The main parts of a pitch document, in order from first to last, are the executive summary, audience analysis, story, competition analysis, market analysis, gameplay, and budget and schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitch writers create collaborative pitch documents often containing design mockups or art concepts. With modern business concerns, include profitability-related metrics such as F.T.U.E. (First Time User Experience) and retention metrics. Use the ordered structure (executive summary → audience → story → competition → market → gameplay → budget/schedule) as the expected scaffold for publisher pitches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative designer remit: story communication and mechanic reinforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative designer is a hybrid role of video game design and writing that creates not only the story, but also how it is communicated to players and how the game mechanics work to reinforce that story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The narrative designer shapes the game's narrative and writes words, but crucially also designs the ways mechanics, level design, and player feedback deliver narrative beats. This role sits at the intersection of design and writing and requires systems thinking about story-mechanics integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Script writing focuses on dialogue and voice-over; use flowcharts for branching
rubrics_metrics.description: The script writer focuses on the dialogue said by characters and the voice over. The script's dialogue can be written in flowcharts to illustrate the various dialogue resulting from both decision and indecision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Script writers are generally less involved with mechanics and more with producing dialogue and voice-over scripts. For branching or choice-driven dialogue, represent conversation trees with flowcharts to track branches and variations that result from player choices or non-choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Script doctoring and ad hoc writing tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Similarly to screenplay script doctors, video game writers can be brought in to assist with writing-related tasks. However, the term is vaguer than in screenplays due to the wide variety of potential tasks needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared for flexible, catch-all assignments: polishing dialogue, reworking story beats to fit new design constraints, revising localization-friendly lines, or fixing narrative inconsistencies late in development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry practice and tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Similar to screenwriting, it is typically a freelance profession. Traditionally, game writers used simple tools like Word, Excel or just plain pen and paper. Some game writers also used tools initially designed for the film industry such as Final Draft. As the field has evolved and player agency started to play a bigger role, the need for professional game writing tools has emerged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect freelance or mixed staffing arrangements; be competent with standard text tools and branching/flowchart tools, and be open to adopting specialized game-writing software as projects demand more complex dialogue and narrative systems.
